e-64.knowledge_point: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide
e-64.problem:
Find the left- and right-sided limits at $x=1$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
{\begin{aligned}6{e}^{x-1}\, & \text{ for }\,x<1 \\ {x}^{2}+2x+3\, & \text{ for }\,x>1.\end{aligned}
$$
e-64.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<1,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = 6e^{x-1}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}6{e}^{x-1} \\  & =6{e}^{1-1} \\  & =6{e}^{0} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>1,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = x^2+2x+3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}{x}^{2}+2x+3 \\  & ={1}^{2}+2(1)+3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the limit at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}6x+1\, & \text{ for }\,x\le \frac{1}{2} \\ -4{log}_{2}⁡x\, & \text{ for }\,x>\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<\frac{1}{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=6x+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{-}}(6x+1) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{2}+1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now,  approaching from the right, we have $x>\frac{1}{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=-4{log}_{2}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{+}}-4{log}_{2}⁡x \\  & =-4{log}_{2}⁡\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-4{log}_{2}⁡{2}^{-1} \\  & =-4(-1){log}_{2}⁡2 \\  & =-4(-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to $4,$ we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to (1/2)}f(x)=4.
$$

Question 1

Find the limit at x=12 of the piecewise function f(x) defined by f(x)={6x+1 for x≤12−4log2⁡x for x>12.

a
limx→(1/2)f(x)=DNE
b
limx→(1/2)f(x)=1
c
limx→(1/2)f(x)=2
d
limx→(1/2)f(x)=4
e
limx→(1/2)f(x)=−4
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Approaching from the left, we have x<12, so we use the expression f(x)=6x+1. We get

limx→(1/2)−f(x)=limx→(1/2)−(6x+1)=6⋅12+1=4.

Now, approaching from the right, we have x>12, so we use the expression f(x)=−4log2⁡x. We get

limx→(1/2)+f(x)=limx→(1/2)+−4log2⁡x=−4log2⁡12=−4log2⁡2−1=−4(−1)log2⁡2=−4(−1)=4.

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to 4, we conclude that limx→(1/2)f(x)=4.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide
content.problem:
Find the limit at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}6x+1\, & \text{ for }\,x\le \frac{1}{2} \\ -4{log}_{2}⁡x\, & \text{ for }\,x>\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<\frac{1}{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=6x+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{-}}(6x+1) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{2}+1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now,  approaching from the right, we have $x>\frac{1}{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=-4{log}_{2}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{+}}-4{log}_{2}⁡x \\  & =-4{log}_{2}⁡\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-4{log}_{2}⁡{2}^{-1} \\  & =-4(-1){log}_{2}⁡2 \\  & =-4(-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to $4,$ we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to (1/2)}f(x)=4.
$$

a
limx→0−f(x)=limx→0+f(x)=1
b

c
limx→0−f(x)=1,limx→0+f(x)=DNE

decision.explanation: From the left, √(-x)+1 approaches √0+1=1. From the right, e^x approaches e^0=1. Both one-sided limits equal 1.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find the left- and right-sided limits at $x=0$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\sqrt{-x}+1 & \text{ for }\,x<0 \\ {e}^{x} & \text{ for }\,x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{-x}+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}(\sqrt{-x}+1) \\  & =\sqrt{-0}+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={e}^{x}.$ We get

$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide
content.problem:
Find the left- and right-sided limits at $x=0$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\sqrt{-x}+1 & \text{ for }\,x<0 \\ {e}^{x} & \text{ for }\,x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{-x}+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}(\sqrt{-x}+1) \\  & =\sqrt{-0}+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={e}^{x}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}{e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{0} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x)=1.
$$
